headline: $800,000 cut from Public Works snow and ice budget, and 35% residential tax exemption set, for FY 2027 taxes.
summary: The cut takes money from the Department of Public Works budget, which drops from $9,525,480 to $8,725,480, and will be raised on the FY 2027 tax recapitulation report. The minimum residential factor is 0.9059, and the presentation put the average residential bill savings at $1,049. A National Grid easement for Forest Dale Cemetery was sent to the Public Properties Committee. An inclusionary zoning ordinance was ordained, and $11,173,912.75 in free cash was referred to Finance.
decisions: Referred the public shade trees paper to Public Properties and Rules and Ordinance together.
Approved the consent agenda: two appointments, one communication filed, and one paper referred.
Approved reducing the FY 2027 Public Works budget by $800,000, 9-1.
Approved the 35% residential exemption and 0.9059 minimum residential factor for FY 2027 tax rates, 10-0.
Referred the $11,173,912.75 free cash transfer to stabilization funds to Finance.
Referred the National Grid easement at Forest Dale Cemetery to the Public Properties Committee.
Approved accepting a $420,000 state park grant for Linden Park playground improvements.
Ordained a revised inclusionary zoning ordinance, Code section 12.12.300.
Ordained a new incentives subsection in the inclusionary zoning code.
Ordained moving animal control officer supervision from the police department to health and inspectional services.
discussion: Snow and ice cut: Members asked why the $800,000 for last winter's snow and ice deficit was taken out of the Public Works budget. They were told the state lets towns run a snow and ice deficit and raise it the next year, and that the cut was needed to set the tax rate.

Residential exemption: Members asked how many residents pay less after the exemption rose to 35%. The presentation said about 8,100 of 12,672 properties qualify for the $3,361 exemption, and a follow-up on the savings from the increase was requested.

Forest Dale Cemetery easement: Public speakers said the cemetery trustees voted to approve the easement while opposed to it, and that trees were harmed and a pole on Forest Street leans. Members suggested a revocable license instead of an easement.

Inclusionary zoning changes: Concerns were raised about conflicts with MBTA zoning and the Overlook Ridge overlay, and a 15% requirement in the MBTA zoning will need changing. A meeting is set for December 1st, and a later paper is expected.
